comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Verified with a forced 5-fail job: requeued message kept attempt_count=5 and first_failed_at within 2s of the original stamp.

content.text: Verified with a forced 5-fail job: requeued message kept attempt_count=5 and first_failed_at within 2s of the original stamp.

When a job exhausts its delivery budget and lands in the dead-letter queue, the requeue path rebuilds the envelope from the DLQ record alone. Operators who then push the job back onto the live queue see attempt_count reset to 0 even though the DLQ row still holds attempt_count=7 and first_failed_at from the original run.

Expected requeue to copy attempt_count, max_attempts, and first_failed_at into the new queue message so downstream dashboards and circuit-breaker logic keep continuity. Actual behavior only restores job_id, payload, and topic; the attempt fields are re-initialized by the publisher defaults.

Suspected cause: dlq_requeue() serializes a fresh JobHeader via DefaultHeader() instead of unmarshaling the stored header blob, so the attempt metadata never leaves cold storage. Impact is skewed retry metrics and premature permanent-failure classification on the second cycle after requeue.
